'''Dmytro Skapintsev''' (born 12 May 1998) is a Ukrainian professional [[basketball]] center and power forward for [[Básquet Coruña]] of the [[Liga ACB]].

==Professional career==
===Early career (2015–22)===
Skapintsev's professional career began with his hometown team, [[BC Cherkaski Mavpy|Cherkaski Mavpy]] in [[Cherkasy]], [[Ukraine]], with whom he played for six years.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.proballers.com/basketball/player/65581/dmytro-skapintsev|title=Dmytro Skapintsev, basketball player|access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref> In 2019, he joined the [[Cal State Northridge Matadors men's basketball|Cal State Northridge Matadors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sundial.csun.edu/155357/sports/a-new-era-is-underway-in-mens-basketball/|title=A New Era is Underway in Men's Basketball|work=Daily Sundial|date=3 November 2019|access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref> He spent a few months with the team, but never appeared in a game.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vorkunov |first1=Mike |title=From Ukraine, to the G League, to the NBA, how Dmytro Skapintsev is making the most of his moment |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/5168091/2023/12/29/ukraine-russia-war-nba-dmytro-skapinstev-knicks/ |website=The Athletic |access-date=13 October 2024 |date=29 December 2023}}</ref>

In 2021, Skapintsev moved to [[BC Kyiv-Basket|Kyiv-Basket]] in Ukraine; he remained with the team through the beginning of 2022. After the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine]] shut down the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]] season, Skapintsev played out the rest of the year with [[BC Pieno žvaigždės|Pieno žvaigždės]], in [[Pasvalys]], [[Lithuania]].

===New York / Westchester Knicks (2022–24)===
On 23 October 2022, Skapintsev signed with the [[Westchester Knicks]], playing out the 2022–23 season with the team.<ref>{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2022-23 Training Camp Roster|url=https://www.oursportscentral.com/services/releases/westchester-knicks-announce-2022-23-training-camp-roster/n-5892760|website=OurSportsCentral.com|date=23 October 2022|access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref>

In July 2023, Skapintsev joined the [[New York Knicks]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League]], and on 3 August, he signed with New York.<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Sign Dmytro Skapintsev to Exhibit 10 Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/knicks/news/knicks-sign-dmytro-skapintsev-to-exhibit-10-contract|website=NBA.com|date=3 August 2023|access-date=6 August 2023}}</ref> However, he was waived on 15 September<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks Waive Dmytro Skapintsev|number=1702781292268363800|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=15 September 2023|access-date=17 September 2023}}</ref> and on 9 November, he was named to the Westchester Knicks opening night roster.<ref>{{cite web|title=Westchester Knicks Announce 2023-24 Official Roster|url=https://westchester.gleague.nba.com/news/westchester-knicks-announce-2023-24-official-roster|website=NBA.com|date=9 November 2023|access-date=3 December 2023}}</ref>

On 23 December 2023, Skapintsev signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[New York Knicks]],<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=.@nyknicks Sign Dmytro Skapintsev to Two-Way Contract|number=1738575387997696192|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=23 December 2023|access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref> and he made his [[NBA]] debut that night in a 130–111 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks beat the Knicks again in a one-sided series, with the teams set to meet again on Christmas|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401585016|website=ESPN.com|date=23 December 2023|access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref> However, he was waived on 1 January 2024, and two days later, he rejoined Westchester.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=NY_KnicksPR|title=Knicks waive Dmytro Skapintsev|number=1741993057342402840|user=NY_KnicksPR|date=1 January 2024|access-date=1 January 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|author=Westchester Knicks|title=Dmytro Skapintsev returns to the Westchester Knicks as a returning rights player.|number=1742668591625891968|user=wcknicks|date=3 January 2024|access-date=4 January 2024}}</ref>

===Maine Celtics (2024–25)===
On 17 September 2024, Skapintsev signed with the [[Boston Celtics]], but he was waived on 16 October./<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Celtics Sign Dmytro Skapintsev To Exhibit 10 Deal|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/09/celtics-dmytro-skapintsev-agree-to-exhibit-10-deal.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=17 September 2024|access-date=18 September 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite tweet|first=Keith|last=Smith|title=The Boston Celtics have waived center Dmytro Skapintsev, a league source told @spotrac.|number=1846669644737675581|user=KeithSmithNBA|date=16 October 2024|access-date=19 October 2024}}</ref> On 26 October, he joined the [[Maine Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Spencer|last=Martin|title=Celtics Select Three In G League Draft|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/draft-training-camp-102624|website=NBA.com|date=26 October 2024|access-date=26 October 2024}}</ref> He played sparingly for the Celtics, appearing in only five games and averaging 3.2 points per game.

===Rip City Remix (2025)===
On 17 January 2025, Skapintsev was traded to the [[Rip City Remix]].<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Rip City Remix|title=The Rip City Remix have acquired center Dmytro Skapintsev from the Maine Celtics in exchange for the returning rights to D'moi Hodge and Daniel Oturu.|number=1880344385084395680|user=ripcityremix|date=17 January 2025|access-date=18 January 2025}}</ref> In 26 games for the team, Skapintsev averaged 10.1 points and 8.2 rebounds.

===Hapoel Jerusalem (2025–2026)===
On 7 August 2025, Skapintsev signed a one-year contract with [[Hapoel Jerusalem B.C.|Hapoel Jerusalem]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Heyen |first=Billy |title= Knicks' former 7-foot-1 center leaves NBA to sign contract in Israel |url= https://sports.yahoo.com/article/knicks-former-7-foot-1-051839686.html |website=[[Yahoo Sports]]|accessdate= 3 September 2025 |date=8 August 2025}}</ref> In 2026-26 in 34 games in 13.8 minutes per game he averaged 5.1 points, 4.5 rebounds, and 0.7 blocks while shooting 64.9% from the field.<ref>[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Dmytro-Skapintsev/Summary/75813 "Dmytro Skapintsev,"] realgm.com.</ref>

===Básquet Coruña (2026–present)===
On 25 July 2026, he signed with [[Básquet Coruña]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Dmytro Skapintsev será la torre del Leyma Coruña en la Liga Endesa |url=https://www.acb.com/es/liga/noticias/dmytro-skapintsev-sera-la-torre-del-leyma-coruna-en-la-liga-endesa-145674 |website=acb.com|accessdate=25 July 2026 |date=25 July 2026 |language=es}}</ref>

==National team career==
Skapintsev was included on [[Ukrainian national basketball team|Ukraine's]] [[EuroBasket 2022 squads|2022 EuroBasket roster]]. He played in two of Ukraine's five group stage games, and did not play in their Round of 16 loss to Poland.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.fiba.basketball/eurobasket/2022/player/Dmytro-Skapintsev|title=Dmytro Skapintsev (UKR)'s profile- FIBA EuroBasket 2022|access-date=17 July 2023}}</ref>
